column1: # Persian for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built into scribe-langs.js by scripts/make-scribe.ps1.
# Two scripts: the Perso-Arabic alphabet of New Persian, and the Old Persian cuneiform of the Achaemenid kings.
# rules=persian: a, e, o inside a word are not written; ā is alef, i and u are ye and vav (also for ey, ow), a final e
# is the silent he (nāme), a word-initial vowel sits on an alef (ā on alef madda). rules=oldpersian (scribe.js): a
# consonant with a or no vowel is its Ca sign; before i or u the Ci or Cu sign where there is one, then the vowel sign;
# long ā adds the sign a; a nasal before a consonant is not written (Kent, Old Persian, 1953, §§ 12–25).

column4: Persian has been written in three scripts: the cuneiform of the Achaemenid kings, scripts drawn from Aramaic for Middle Persian, and since the 9th century the Arabic alphabet with four letters of its own.

column2: New Persian in the Arabic script, with پ چ ژ گ added for sounds Arabic lacks; the alphabet of Ferdowsi, Rumi and Hafez, and of Persian today.

Type as it sounds: sh, ch, zh, kh, gh for ش چ ژ خ غ. Long ā becomes ا, i and u become ی and و; short a, e and o inside a word are not written, and a final e is the silent ه (nāme). The letters that Persian took from Arabic are on the keys, with the sound they have in Persian.

column4: alef · a long a, or the seat of a first vowel
eyn · a catch in the throat
vāv · v; also u and o
he · h; also a final e

column2: A script of 36 sound signs, a few word signs and a word divider, made for the Achaemenid kings in the 6th century BCE and carved at Behistun, Persepolis and Susa.

Type the words as they were said; the rules of the script are applied for you: a consonant before i or u keeps its own sign where it has one (di, mi, ju …), long ā adds the sign a, and n before a consonant is left out. Type a word sign in capitals: XŠ king, DH land, BG god, BU earth, AM Ahuramazda. Spaces become the slanting word divider.

column4: ça · a sound between s and th
